fields.lr_title: Emergency lock and door opening in Bilbao: what to know before calling a locksmith
fields.lr_lead: If your front door will not open, the first step is to work out what the problem is and avoid damaging the lock with improvised attempts. Below we explain how emergency door opening works, when a mechanism needs replacing and what to have ready before the locksmith arrives.
fields.lr_body:
Can a door be opened without damaging the lock?

In many cases the front door can be opened while keeping the lock and the door leaf intact. The result depends on how the door is built, the type of cylinder, the condition of the mechanism and the reason it is blocked. For example, a door that has slammed shut and a faulty multi-point lock need different approaches.

The Cerrajero24 locksmith first inspects the door and assesses whether it can be opened without damage. If restoring access means damaging or replacing some parts, the specialist will explain the situation and agree the steps with you before starting. Find out more on the emergency door opening page.

What to do if your front door is jammed?

Do not force the key, hit the lock or try to prise the door open with whatever is at hand. This can make the fault worse, damage the cylinder and increase the cost of the repair. Check whether a sagging door leaf is stopping it from closing and whether the key shows any signs of damage.

If the mechanism still does not work, contact a locksmith. Tell them whether the key turns, whether the handle opens the door and what kind of lock you have. With this information the specialist can assess the job in advance. If the cause is a worn mechanism, a door lock repair will help.

When does a lock need replacing after opening?

You do not have to replace the lock after every emergency opening. If the mechanism is sound and the door was opened without damage, it is usually enough to check it works. Replacement may be needed if the cylinder is worn, a key has broken inside, the mechanism is damaged or it keeps sticking.

Losing your keys or moving into a new flat is a different matter. Even if the door opens normally, a new cylinder ensures nobody can use old sets of keys. The locksmith will tell you whether replacing the cylinder is enough or the whole lock needs changing. Find out more about lock and cylinder replacement.

How to prepare for the locksmith’s visit?

When you call, give your address in Bilbao or Biscay and the type of property, and briefly describe the problem: the door slammed shut, the keys are lost, the lock is jammed or the key is damaged. If you can, send a photo of the door and the lock — it helps with a preliminary estimate.

Have a document or other proof of your right to access the property ready. If your documents are inside, let the dispatcher know in advance. Before starting, the locksmith will check that you are authorised, inspect the lock and agree the price and any additional costs. You can send a request using the form below or by phone.
fields.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about emergency lock opening in Bilbao
fields.faq_help_text: Contact a locksmith — we’ll answer and tell you what to do right now.

faq_items.q: How much does emergency lock opening cost in Bilbao?
faq_items.a: Emergency door lock opening costs from €45, car opening from €45 and safe opening from €60. The final price depends on the type of door and lock, the time of day and the area; the dispatcher will tell you the call-out fee when you call. The locksmith gives the exact amount after inspecting the lock and before starting work — he will not begin without your consent.

faq_items.q: How long does it take for the locksmith to arrive?
faq_items.a: It depends on the area, the time of day and how busy the on-call locksmiths are. The dispatcher gives you an approximate arrival time as soon as you call and warns you in advance if the locksmith is delayed. We reach central Bilbao districts fastest. Travel to more distant Greater Bilbao municipalities, such as Muskiz or Larrabetzu, takes longer.

faq_items.q: Can a front door be opened without damage?
faq_items.a: In most cases, yes — especially if the door has slammed shut on the latch and the cylinder is in good condition. With armoured doors and high-security locks it is sometimes impossible to save the mechanism. We aim to open the lock without damage, and if that is not possible, we explain why beforehand and agree the next steps and the price with you.

faq_items.q: Is the lock opening service available 24 hours a day?
faq_items.a: Yes. We take requests and come out 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including weekends and public holidays. At night, from 22:00 to 08:00, and at weekends and on holidays a surcharge applies — the dispatcher tells you the amount when you call, before the locksmith sets off.

faq_items.q: Can you open a flat if the keys are inside?
faq_items.a: Yes, it’s one of the most common situations. If the door has slammed shut with the key left in the lock on the inside, the locksmith will choose the method that suits that particular case. After opening, we will ask you to show a document proving you live at the address: DNI, NIE, a rental contract or a utility bill.

faq_items.q: What should I do if the key breaks in the lock?
faq_items.a: Do not try to pull the broken piece out with a hairpin or glue: you could push it further in and damage the cylinder. If the door is open, do not close it. Call a locksmith: he will extract the piece with a special tool, check the mechanism and, if the cylinder is damaged, offer to replace it on the spot. Key extraction costs from €60.

faq_items.q: What documents are needed to open a flat or a car?
faq_items.a: For a flat or house, a photo ID (DNI, NIE or passport) and proof of your link to the address: a certificate of registration (empadronamiento), a rental contract, an escritura (title deed) or a utility bill. For a car, the permiso de circulación (vehicle registration) or other vehicle documents. If the documents are inside, we check them straight after opening. In doubtful situations we work in the presence of the police.

faq_items.q: How much does it cost to open a lock at night?
faq_items.a: From 22:00 to 08:00, and at weekends and on public holidays, a surcharge is added to the base price; the amount depends on the time and the complexity of the work. We tell you the full amount, surcharge included, when you call — before the locksmith sets off — so a night call-out doesn’t end in an unexpected bill.

faq_items.q: Can the lock be replaced straight after opening?
faq_items.a: Yes. The locksmith carries popular cylinders and locks with different security ratings, so we usually replace them during the same visit. If your door needs a special model, for example for an armoured door, we will source it and arrange a second visit. We tell you the price of the parts before fitting them.

faq_items.q: Do you open armoured doors and electronic locks?
faq_items.a: Yes, we work with armoured doors (puertas acorazadas), multi-point, combination and electronic locks. These are more complex jobs: prices start at €150 and depend on the model and security rating. For an electronic lock, tell us the model and what exactly is wrong — a flat battery, a malfunction or a mechanical fault.

faq_items.q: Can I get a price in advance from a photo?
faq_items.a: Yes. Send a photo of the lock from both sides of the door via the website form or WhatsApp and briefly describe the situation. The photos are easy to take on your phone: outside, a close-up of the cylinder; inside, the handle and the latch. The locksmith will identify the type of mechanism and give you an approximate price. The final price is confirmed on site after inspection — before work begins.

faq_items.q: Do your locksmiths work outside Bilbao?
faq_items.a: Yes, we work in all 26 municipalities of Greater Bilbao: on the Left Bank (Barakaldo, Sestao, Portugalete, Santurtzi), on the Right Bank (Getxo, Leioa, Erandio), in the Asua valley, in Basauri, Galdakao and others. The call-out fee outside Bilbao depends on the distance — the dispatcher will tell you when you call.

fields.lr_title: What to do if you can’t open your flat’s front door?
fields.lr_lead: When the door won’t open, the main thing is not to damage the lock or the door leaf. Here’s how to assess the situation before the locksmith arrives, when the lock can be saved and what to have ready.
fields.lr_body:
What to do if the door has slammed shut with the keys inside?

First check whether there is another way in: a spare set with relatives, neighbours or the building manager. Don’t try to prise the door open with a knife, a plastic card or a screwdriver — it’s easy to damage the door leaf, the seal and the latch, and the call-out will cost more.

Call a locksmith and tell them whether the door is just on the latch or locked with a key — the opening method depends on it. See the price table for guide prices.

Why won’t the key turn in the door lock?

The most common causes are a worn cylinder, dirt in the mechanism, a bent key or a sagging door that makes the bolt catch on the strike plate. Sometimes the lock jams after someone tries to open it with the wrong key.

Don’t use force: a key broken in the cylinder will make opening harder. The locksmith will find the exact cause during diagnosis. If the cause is wear, a door lock repair will help.

Can a flat be opened without replacing the lock?

Yes, if the mechanism is sound and the door has slammed shut on the latch or is locked with a standard cylinder. Replacement is needed when the cylinder is broken or worn, a piece of key is stuck inside or the lock cannot be opened any other way.

In that case, the locksmith explains in advance why the mechanism cannot be saved and tells you the price of a new cylinder. Find out more in the opening without damage section.

Should you change the lock after losing your keys?

Getting back into your flat and keeping it secure are two different things. If your keys were lost together with documents or a key ring showing your address, a stranger could use them.

In that case it’s best to replace the cylinder straight away: it’s quicker and cheaper than replacing the whole lock, and the old keys will no longer work. Find out more about lock cylinder replacement.

What should you have ready before the locksmith arrives?

The exact address with the floor and entry code, a short description of the problem and, if possible, a photo of the lock from outside — it makes it easier to estimate the price in advance. Have a document proving your right of access ready: DNI, NIE or passport and a document with your address. If your documents are inside, let the dispatcher know — the locksmith will check them straight after opening. See which documents are accepted in the documents section.
fields.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about emergency flat opening
fields.faq_help_text: Contact a locksmith — we’ll answer and tell you what to do right now.

faq_items.q: How much does emergency flat opening cost in Bilbao?
faq_items.a: The price depends on the type of door and lock, the reason the door won’t open, the time of the call-out and the address. You’ll find guide prices for the most common situations in the price table. The dispatcher gives you an approximate price by phone, and the locksmith gives the final price after inspecting the lock and before starting. No work begins without your consent.

faq_items.q: How quickly will a locksmith arrive to open the door?
faq_items.a: Arrival time depends on the area, the time of day and how busy the on-call locksmiths are. The dispatcher gives you an approximate time as soon as you call and lets you know if the locksmith is delayed. We reach central Bilbao districts fastest — Abando, Indautxu, Casco Viejo; travel to Greater Bilbao municipalities usually takes longer.

faq_items.q: Can the front door be opened without damaging the lock?
faq_items.a: Usually yes — especially if the door has slammed shut on the latch and the cylinder is in good condition. With armoured doors and high-security cylinders it is sometimes impossible to save the mechanism. We aim to open the door without damage, and if that is not possible, we explain why in advance and agree a replacement with you. Find out more in the opening without damage section.

faq_items.q: What to do if your keys are inside the flat?
faq_items.a: Don’t try to force the door or the lock: you could damage the door leaf and make opening harder. Call a locksmith and say whether the door is locked with a key or has just slammed shut, and whether the key is in the lock on the inside. Have a document proving your address ready — if it is inside, the locksmith will check it straight after opening.

faq_items.q: Do you open flats at night?
faq_items.a: Yes, the service runs around the clock, including weekends and public holidays. At night from 22:00 to 08:00 and on public holidays a surcharge applies — the dispatcher tells you the amount when you call, before the locksmith sets off. At night it is faster to call than to send a request through the website. If someone inside the flat is in danger or there is a fire risk, call the emergency services on 112 first.

faq_items.q: How long does it take to open a front door?
faq_items.a: The quickest door to open is one that has simply slammed shut on the latch, with a standard cylinder in good condition. An armoured door, a multi-point lock or a piece of key stuck in the cylinder takes longer. The locksmith will be more precise after inspecting it. If the cylinder needs replacing, add the time to fit a new one — usually during the same visit.

faq_items.q: Can an armoured door be opened?
faq_items.a: Yes, our locksmiths work with armoured doors (puertas acorazadas) and multi-point locks. These doors are designed to resist opening, so the work is more complex and the mechanism cannot always be saved. Before starting, the locksmith assesses the door and agrees the opening method and price with you. Find out more about door types in the doors and locks section.

faq_items.q: What should I do if the key breaks in the lock?
faq_items.a: Don’t try to get the broken piece out with a hairpin, glue or another key — it’s easy to push it further in and damage the cylinder. If the door is open, don’t close it. The locksmith will extract the piece with a special tool, check the mechanism and, if the cylinder is damaged, replace it on the spot. Find out more about broken key extraction.

faq_items.q: Do you need to change the lock after an emergency opening?
faq_items.a: Not necessarily. If the door was opened without damage and the mechanism is sound, it’s enough to check it works. Replacement is needed if the cylinder is damaged or worn, and also if you have lost your keys — so nobody can use the old set. The locksmith will tell you whether replacing the cylinder is enough or a new lock is needed.

faq_items.q: What documents are needed to open a flat?
faq_items.a: A photo ID (DNI, NIE or passport) and proof of your link to the address: empadronamiento, escritura, a rental contract or a utility bill. A tenant just needs the rental contract and a photo ID. If the documents are inside, the locksmith will check them straight after opening. Find out more in the documents section.

faq_items.q: Can I find out the price in advance from a photo?
faq_items.a: Yes. Send a photo of the door and lock via WhatsApp and briefly describe the problem. The locksmith will identify the type of mechanism and give you an approximate price. Two photos work best: a close-up of the cylinder and the whole door. The final price is confirmed on site after inspection — before work begins.

faq_items.q: Do you cover the Bilbao suburbs?
faq_items.a: Yes. As well as every district of Bilbao, we cover the municipalities of Greater Bilbao: Barakaldo, Getxo, Portugalete, Santurtzi, Leioa, Sestao, Basauri, Erandio and others. The price and arrival time outside the city depend on the distance — the dispatcher will tell you when you call. You can check your area on the service area map.

fields.lr_title: What to do if your keys are locked in the car?
fields.lr_lead: A locked car with the keys inside is a nuisance, but it’s usually sorted in a single locksmith visit. Here’s what to check yourself, what not to do and how to prepare for the specialist’s arrival.
fields.lr_body:
Keys left in the car: what to check first?

Walk around the car and try all the doors and the boot: sometimes one door stays unlocked. If you have a spare key — at home, with relatives or colleagues — it can be quicker to bring it than to wait for a locksmith.

Don’t try to open the door with a wire, a ruler or a screwdriver: it’s easy to damage the seal, the lock linkages and the window motor wiring. Repairs after such an attempt cost more than the opening. See the price table for guide prices.

Why won’t the car open with the remote?

Most often the remote’s battery is flat: the buttons stop working even though the key itself is fine. Many remotes hide a mechanical key — you can slide it out and open the driver’s door through the cylinder, if there is one.

If neither the remote nor the cylinder responds, the cause may be a flat car battery or a faulty door lock. Call a locksmith: based on your description, he’ll tell you what to check.

Can a car be opened without damage?

Don’t try to get the broken piece out with another key, a hairpin or glue: it’s easy to push it further in. The locksmith will extract it with a special tool and check the cylinder. Find out more about broken key extraction.

fields.lr_title: What to do if your safe won’t open?
fields.lr_lead: When a safe won’t open, the key thing is not to make matters worse: many safes lock out after several wrong attempts, and brute force can jam the mechanism for good. Here’s what to check yourself and when to call a locksmith.
fields.lr_body:
What to do if you’ve forgotten the safe code?

Don’t try combinations one after another: many electronic safes lock out for a while after several wrong attempts, and repeated errors extend the lockout. Look for the manual and your notes — many models have a master code or an emergency key.

If you have neither the code nor the emergency key, call a locksmith and give the make and model of the safe — they’re usually shown on the door. The model makes it easier to tell whether the safe can be opened without damage.

Why won’t the electronic safe respond to the buttons?

Most often the batteries are flat. Many models have an external emergency power connector or a back-up mechanical key under a decorative cover. If emergency power can’t be connected, the locksmith will open the safe and replace the batteries.

If the safe beeps but won’t open, the electronics may have failed or the bolt may have jammed. Don’t bang the door or yank the handle — it’s easy to damage the mechanism.

Can a safe be opened without drilling?

Yes, if its design allows it: with flat batteries, a back-up key or a working mechanical combination lock. High-grade burglar-resistant safes are designed to resist opening, and the lock can’t always be saved.

If drilling can’t be avoided, the locksmith will explain why in advance and tell you the price of a new lock. Find out more in the opening without damage section.

What to do after the safe has been opened?

Set a new code and check the lock works. If the lock had to be drilled, fit a new one — otherwise the safe will no longer protect its contents. Write the code down and keep the note away from the safe.

If the safe keys were lost together with your house keys, also think about replacing the front door cylinder.

What to have ready before the locksmith arrives?

The make and model of the safe, a photo of its door and lock, the address and a convenient time. Have a photo ID ready and proof of your right to the safe or the property. If the safe is built into a wall or wardrobe, let the dispatcher know. See which documents are accepted in the documents section.

fields.lr_title: What to do if your garage won’t open?
fields.lr_lead: Garage doors usually fail at the worst moment — just when you need to drive off. Here’s what you can check yourself, what not to do and when it’s time to call a locksmith.
fields.lr_body:
Why won’t the key turn in the garage lock?

Garage and shutter locks are outdoors or in damp basements, so they suffer more from dirt, moisture and rust. The cylinder clogs up, and the bolt can seize to the strike plate.

Don’t use force or try to turn the key with pliers: a broken key will make opening harder. If the lock is just sticking, a lock repair will help; if the key has already broken, you need broken key extraction.

What to do if the door doesn’t respond to the remote?

First check the remote’s battery and whether there’s power in the garage. If the motor isn’t working, most doors have a manual release — usually a cord or lever on the motor inside the garage, and on some models a lock outside.

If you can’t reach the release, the locksmith will help you open the door manually. Repairing the motor and remotes is a job for door automation specialists.

Can a metal shutter be opened without damage?

Usually yes: if the problem is the lock, it is opened or replaced without touching the shutter. It’s harder if the shutter is twisted or has come off its tracks — then the locksmith will assess whether it can be fixed on the spot. Find out more in the opening without damage section.

Should the garage lock be changed after losing the keys?

If the keys were lost together with documents or a key ring that could lead someone to your garage, it’s best to change the cylinder or padlock. It’s quick and inexpensive, and the old keys will no longer work. Find out more about lock and cylinder replacement.

What to have ready before the locksmith arrives?

The address, the type of door and lock and, if possible, a photo. If the garage is in a communal car park or the storage room is in a basement, tell us how the locksmith can get in. Have a photo ID ready and proof of your right to the garage. See which documents are accepted in the documents section.

fields.lr_title: What to do if your office or shop won’t open?
fields.lr_lead: A locked shop or office means missed meetings and lost customers. Here’s how to quickly assess the situation, what to prepare for the locksmith and how to protect the premises after losing the keys.
fields.lr_body:
Office door won’t open: what to check first?

Try all the keys on the bunch and ask colleagues who has a spare set. Check whether the door is locked from inside with a second lock or bolt — this happens if the last person left through the service entrance.

Don’t force the key: a key broken in the cylinder will make opening harder. Call a locksmith and describe what’s happening with the lock. See the price table for guide prices.

Why does a metal shutter lock jam?

Metal shutter locks (cierres metálicos) are outdoors: dirt, water and sand get into them. The mechanism gradually wears out, and one day the key stops turning.

To prevent this, clean the shutter lock from time to time and lubricate it with a dry lubricant. If it’s already sticking, a lock repair will help — before it jams completely.

What to do if an employee loses the keys or leaves?

Replace the cylinders as soon as possible: it’s inexpensive and quick, and the old keys will no longer work. If the premises have several doors, you can fit cylinders keyed alike.

Find out more about choosing cylinders on the lock and cylinder replacement page.

What to do after a break-in attempt?

Don’t touch the door or lock and call the police on 112 straight away. Photograph the damage: the photos and the police report (denuncia) will be needed for the insurance claim.

Once the damage has been recorded, the locksmith will open the premises, replace the damaged lock and suggest how to improve security — for example, by fitting an extra lock.

What to have ready before the locksmith arrives?

The exact address, the type of door and locks and the contact details of whoever will meet the locksmith. Have a photo ID ready and proof of your right to the premises. If you’re an employee, let the owner know — the locksmith may ask them to confirm the job. See which documents are accepted in the documents section.

fields.lr_title: Why do door locks break, and how can you make them last longer?
fields.lr_lead: A lock rarely breaks without warning: it usually gives signs for weeks or months. Here’s what to look out for, what you can do yourself and when it’s time to call a locksmith.
fields.lr_body:
Why is the key hard to turn in the lock?

The most common causes are dirt and dust in the cylinder, a worn key or pins, and a misaligned door. In Bilbao, damp adds to this: in older buildings and in locks exposed to the weather, the mechanism oxidises faster.

Don’t use oil or multi-purpose sprays — they help for a couple of weeks and then collect dust. Cylinders need a graphite- or PTFE-based dry lubricant. If that doesn’t help, the lock needs a diagnosis.

Why does the door take effort to close?

Most often the door, not the lock, is the problem: it drops on its hinges or warps with damp, and the bolt starts to hit the strike plate. Forcing a door like this wears the lock out quickly.

The locksmith will adjust the hinges or reposition the strike plate — it’s inexpensive and usually quick. Find out more in the section on repair and replacement.

When is it better to repair a lock, and when to replace it?

A repair makes sense if the cause is dirt, adjustment or a single broken part. Replacement is needed if the cylinder is badly worn, the keys are lost or the lock has been discontinued and parts are no longer available.

If you’ve been meaning to improve your door’s security, a breakdown is a good moment to fit an anti-bump, anti-drill cylinder. Find out more about lock and cylinder replacement.

What should I do if the lock has jammed and the door won’t open?

Don’t try to turn the key with pliers — it may snap inside. Call a locksmith: they’ll open the door and repair or replace the lock in the same visit. Find out more about emergency flat opening.

How can I make a lock last longer?

Once a year, clean the cylinder and treat it with a dry lubricant, don’t hang a heavy bunch of keys from the key in the lock and don’t slam the door. If the key starts to turn harder, don’t wait for the lock to jam: an early repair costs less.

fields.lr_title: How do you know it’s time to replace a lock or cylinder?
fields.lr_lead: The cylinder is the most vulnerable part of a door: it’s where burglars most often try to force the lock, and it’s also the first part to wear out. Here’s when it’s worth replacing it and how to choose a new one.
fields.lr_body:
What’s the difference between replacing the cylinder and replacing the lock?

The cylinder (bombín) is the removable part of the lock that the key goes into. It can be replaced without removing the whole lock — faster and cheaper. The whole lock is replaced if the case or bolts are broken, or if you want to switch to another system, such as a multi-point lock.

When must the cylinder be replaced?

After losing your keys if your address may have gone missing with them; after moving into a flat you’ve bought or rented; when former occupants, employees or tenants still have keys; after a break-in attempt. In all these cases, a new cylinder makes the old keys useless.

If your keys are lost and the door is locked, the locksmith opens it first and then fits a new cylinder straight away. Find out more about emergency flat opening.

What is bumping, and how can you protect against it?

Bumping is a way of opening standard cylinders with a specially cut key blank. It leaves almost no trace, which makes it dangerous. Anti-bump cylinders (antibumping) are designed so that this method doesn’t work on them.

When choosing, also look for protection against drilling (antitaladro), extraction (antiextracción) and snapping (antirrotura). Find out more in the section on choosing a cylinder.

How do I measure a cylinder for replacement?

A cylinder is measured from the central fixing screw on the door edge to each end. Typical sizes are 30×30, 30×35 and 30×40 mm. The locksmith measures it on the spot and chooses the right one: the cylinder shouldn’t stick out noticeably from the door or escutcheon.

Can I replace the lock in a rented flat?

Yes, but it’s best to let the landlord know. Good practice is to keep the old cylinder and, when you move out, put it back or give the landlord the keys to the new one. If the lock breaks through wear, its repair is usually agreed with the landlord. Find out more in the section on documents.

fields.lr_title: Which lock should I fit to my front door?
fields.lr_lead: A good lock means a reliable mechanism, correct fitting and protection for the door’s weak points. Here’s what to look for when choosing.
fields.lr_body:
Mortice or surface-mounted lock: which should I choose?

A mortice lock (de embutir) is fitted inside the door leaf and can’t be seen from outside — it’s the main lock on most front doors. A surface-mounted lock or bolt (de sobreponer, cerrojo) is fixed to the inside of the door.

In Spain, a surface-mounted bolt is often fitted as a second lock: it makes the door harder to force and doesn’t require major changes to the door. The locksmith will advise which option suits your door.

Do I need a second lock on my front door?

Two locks of different designs make a door much harder to force: each needs its own method and time. If the main lock is a cylinder lock, the second is often a bolt or a lock with a different type of mechanism.

What is a security escutcheon for?

The cylinder is the most vulnerable part of a lock: burglars try to drill it, snap it or pull it out. A security escutcheon (escudo de seguridad) covers the cylinder with a steel plate and protects it against these methods.

Together with an escutcheon, it’s worth fitting an anti-bump, anti-drill cylinder. Find out more about lock and cylinder replacement.

Can a lock be fitted to any door?

Almost any door, but not any lock. A thin leaf, glass or a hollow-core door limits the choice: a large lock can’t always be morticed into them. The locksmith will inspect the door and suggest options that won’t weaken it.

If the door is misaligned, it’s adjusted first — otherwise the new lock will stick. Find out more in the section on how we install locks.

What should I prepare before the locksmith’s visit?

Photos of the door from both sides and of the edge where the current lock is, and a rough budget. If you want a particular model, tell us which — the locksmith will check whether it’s suitable. If the door is a building entrance or in a shared area, get the owners’ association’s approval beforehand. Find out more in the section on documents.

fields.lr_title: What should I do if the key breaks in the lock?
fields.lr_lead: A snapped key is a common problem, and it’s most often made worse by trying to get the piece out yourself. Here’s what to do straight away and what’s best avoided.
fields.lr_body:
Why do keys snap in the lock?

Most often through wear: over time the key thins and cracks near the bow. Another cause is trying to force the key when the lock is sticking. Thin mailbox and padlock keys snap especially often.

If the key starts to turn stiffly, don’t wait for it to snap: clean and lubricate the lock or book a lock repair.

What should you avoid if the key has snapped?

Don’t put the spare key into the lock — it will push the piece in further. Don’t try to get the piece out with glue: it will set inside the mechanism and the cylinder will have to be replaced. Hairpins, needles and tweezers damage the pins more often than they help.

If the door is open, don’t close it until the piece has been removed.

Can the cylinder be saved after key extraction?

Yes, if the mechanism isn’t damaged. A piece that snapped through wear and wasn’t pushed in usually comes out without damage. If the cylinder is damaged, the locksmith will suggest replacing it in the same visit. Find out more in the section on extraction without replacing the cylinder.

Can a new key be cut from the broken pieces?

For standard keys, often yes: a key-cutting shop can make a copy from the two parts. High-security keys can only be copied with the owner’s card. If you have no keys left, it’s safer to replace the cylinder.

What to have ready before the locksmith arrives?

Tell the dispatcher where the key snapped — in a door, mailbox, car or garage — and whether the door is locked. Keep the other half of the key and have your spare ready if you have one. If the door is locked, you’ll need a photo ID and proof of address. Find out more in the section on documents.
fields.faq_title: Frequently asked questions about key extraction
fields.faq_help_text: Contact a locksmith — we’ll answer and tell you what to do right now.

faq_items.q: How much does broken key extraction cost in Bilbao?
faq_items.a: The price depends on where the key snapped, how deep the piece is and whether the cylinder needs replacing. See the price table for guide prices. The locksmith gives you the final price after inspecting the lock and before work starts.

faq_items.q: Can I get the broken piece out myself?
faq_items.a: Sometimes — if the piece is sticking out and can be carefully hooked out. But attempts to push it or pull it out with glue more often damage the cylinder. If the piece is inside, it’s better to call a locksmith.

faq_items.q: Does the cylinder need replacing after key extraction?
faq_items.a: Not necessarily. If the mechanism isn’t damaged, the lock will keep working with the spare key. Replacement is needed if the cylinder is damaged or there’s no spare key.

faq_items.q: What should I do if the key has snapped and the door is locked?
faq_items.a: Call a locksmith: they’ll remove the piece and open the door. Have a photo ID and proof of address ready — if the documents are inside, the locksmith will check them after opening.

faq_items.q: Do you extract keys from mailboxes?
faq_items.a: Yes, it’s a common call-out. Mailbox locks are small and the piece usually comes out quickly. If the lock is damaged, it can be replaced.

faq_items.q: What should I do if the key is stuck and won’t come out?
faq_items.a: Don’t pull or force the key to turn — it may snap. Call a locksmith: they’ll carefully remove the key and check the mechanism.

faq_items.q: Can a new key be cut from the broken pieces?
faq_items.a: For standard keys, often yes: a key-cutting shop makes the copy from the two parts. High-security keys need the owner’s card.

faq_items.q: Do you work at night?
faq_items.a: Yes, around the clock, including weekends and public holidays. A surcharge applies at night and on public holidays — the dispatcher will tell you the amount when you call.

faq_items.q: How long does key extraction take?
faq_items.a: Usually not long if the piece hasn’t been pushed in deep. If the cylinder needs replacing or the door needs opening, that adds time for those jobs.

faq_items.q: Do you cover the Bilbao suburbs?
faq_items.a: Yes. As well as every district of Bilbao, we cover the municipalities of Greater Bilbao: Barakaldo, Getxo, Portugalete, Santurtzi, Leioa, Sestao, Basauri, Erandio and others. The dispatcher will tell you the price and arrival time outside the city when you call. You can check your area on the service area map.

fields.faq_help_text: Call us — the on-call locksmith is available around the clock.

faq_items.q: What is the fastest way to call a locksmith?
faq_items.a: Call +34 944 123 456. Calling is the fastest option: the dispatcher will confirm the address and situation straight away, give you an approximate price and arrival time and pass the job to the on-call locksmith. We also handle requests from the website and WhatsApp messages, but if the problem is urgent, it is better to call.

faq_items.q: Can I message on WhatsApp instead of calling?
faq_items.a: Yes. Message us on WhatsApp with what happened and your address, and attach a photo of the lock — a photo makes it easier to identify the mechanism and give you an approximate price. A reply by message may take a little longer than a call, so if you can’t get into your home right now, it is better to call.

faq_items.q: Do you take calls at night, at weekends and on holidays?
faq_items.a: Yes, the line is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including public holidays. At night, from 22:00 to 08:00, and at weekends and on holidays there is a surcharge for urgent call-outs. The dispatcher tells you the amount when you call, before the locksmith sets off, so there are no surprises with the price.

faq_items.q: Which areas do your locksmiths cover?
faq_items.a: Every district of Bilbao — Abando, Deusto, Begoña, Uribarri, Errekalde and others — and the Greater Bilbao municipalities on both banks of the Nervión: Barakaldo, Getxo, Portugalete, Santurtzi, Sestao, Leioa, Basauri, Galdakao and others. You can check your area on the service area map on this page.

faq_items.q: Can I find out the price before the locksmith arrives?
faq_items.a: An approximate one, yes. The dispatcher gives it to you over the phone if you describe the situation and the type of door and lock, and a photo of the lock makes the estimate more accurate. The locksmith gives the final price after an on-site inspection and before starting, and work only begins with your consent. You will find guide prices in the price table.

faq_items.q: How can I leave a review or ask about completed work?
faq_items.a: You can leave a review on our Google Maps profile — the link is in the “Company details” section. Questions about completed work, the guarantee or documents are best sent to info@cerrajero24.es: include the date of the call-out, the address and the phone number you called from, so we can find your job faster.
